page.title: Gamebook Framework: write gamebooks, play anywhere
page.description: An open JSON format for gamebooks with stats, dice, items and combat built in. Play and edit stories right in your browser.

play.title: Write a story, play it at once
play.lead: Edit the JSON on the Edit tab. After every change the real engine checks your story and, if nothing is broken, starts a new game on the Play tab.
play.step1: Open Edit JSON and change a text, an item or a number.
play.step2: Read the checker: errors say where the problem is, like nodes.door.choices[0].
play.step3: Switch to Play to try it. Download keeps your work; Open file loads a story from your computer.
player.cannotPlay: Fix the errors on the Edit tab to play again.

home.data.title: No scripting language to learn
home.data.p1: A gamebook is a graph of pages. Here every page, choice, condition, dice check and fight is plain data, so editors, scripts and AI can write it, and a validator can prove every link leads somewhere before a reader ever gets stuck.
home.data.p2: The Rusty Door below is the whole format in one screen: an item, a locked choice and a dice check. Open Edit JSON and change the target number from 15 to 5.
home.features.title: Everything a gamebook needs, built in
home.f1.title: Pages and choices
home.f1.text: Branching pages with victory and death endings. Choices can be hidden, greyed out with a reason, or vanish once taken.
home.f2.title: Items and the pack
home.f2.text: Keys that unlock choices, potions you use, swords that add to Skill, a pack with limited room, containers, swaps, even thieves.
home.f3.title: Stats and heroes
home.f3.text: Fighting Fantasy and d20-lite presets, or your own stats. Roll the hero, reroll, name them and pick starting kit.
home.f4.title: Dice and checks
home.f4.text: Any dice: 1d6, 2d6+6, 1d20. Pass or fail checks against a number or a stat, Test your Luck, and random outcome tables.
home.f5.title: Combat
home.f5.text: Round by round, opposed or versus defense, several enemies at once, armor, fleeing, luck in fights and Lone Wolf results tables.
home.f6.title: A living world
home.f6.text: Flags, visit counts and conditions change what pages say and which choices open. Live numbers in text: “You have {gold} gold.”
home.f7.title: Journal, audio, achievements
home.f7.text: Unlockable journal entries, looping music and sound effects, and achievements that last across games.
home.f8.title: Any language
home.f8.text: One file per language with the same ids. The validator checks that every translation has the same pages, items and choices.
home.f9.title: Writer friendly
home.f9.text: Page titles, author notes, chapters and draft pages for work in progress, and one-file .gamebook packages to share.
home.compare.title: Built for gamebooks, not just branching text
home.compare.lead: Ink and Twine are excellent for branching prose. Gamebooks also need stats, dice, inventory and combat, and those usually end up hand-coded for each game.
home.compare.twine2: No: it outputs a web page
home.compare.gf2: Yes: any language can parse it
home.compare.honest: The trade-off: raw JSON is less pleasant to write than Ink for long prose, and there is no visual editor in this repository yet. The validator, the JSON Schema and this site's live editor make up for much of it.
home.tools.title: Catch mistakes before your readers do
home.t1.title: Validator
home.t1.text: Broken links, unreachable pages, items never given, bad dice, mismatched translations, each with the exact place in the file.
home.t2.title: Story graph
home.t2.text: Draw the whole story as a map, in Graphviz or Mermaid.
home.t3.title: Simulator
home.t3.text: Plays your story thousands of times at random to find dead ends, loops and endings nobody reaches.
home.t4.title: Packages
home.t4.text: Zip a game folder with its images and audio into one .gamebook file players can import.
home.t5.title: Twine import
home.t5.text: Bring a Twine story over, with a report of what could not be converted.
home.t6.title: LLM kit
home.t6.text: A compact guide to the format for AI assistants, so they write valid stories.
home.t7.title: JSON Schema
home.t7.text: Autocomplete and inline errors in any editor that understands JSON Schema.
home.t8.title: Conformance suite
home.t8.text: Language-neutral test cases, so an engine in TypeScript, Python or C# plays every story exactly like the reference.
home.end.title: Your first gamebook is ten minutes away
home.end.lead: Start the tutorial or open the playground, change a page and play it. No install, no account.
